=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- tests/test_implement_plan_claude_command.py
  Line or code reference: line 34
  Problem: The assertion `assert "only a \`success\` run has audited anything" in text` uses `\`` (backslash-backtick) in the Python string literal. In Python, backtick is not a recognized escape sequence, so `\`` produces two literal characters: backslash (U+005C) followed by backtick (U+0060). The command file at line 32 contains `only a `success` run has audited anything` with plain backtick characters (U+0060) and no backslashes. The `text` fixture does `" ".join(text.split())` which normalizes whitespace but preserves punctuation characters as-is. The search string with backslash-backtick pairs never matches the normalized command text with plain backtick characters.
  Why it fails at runtime: pytest raises `AssertionError` because the string `only a \`success\` run has audited anything` (containing literal backslash characters before each backtick) is absent from the fixture's normalized text. The phrase `only a `success` run has audited anything` (with plain backtick U+0060 characters, matching line 32 of the command file) IS present in the text, but the test's escaped version will not match. This is a concrete CI failure on every PR.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
